name: Pointwise energy conditions NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC and 'the DEC requires the WEC' (merged: weak-energy-condition-pointwise)

source.located: Hawking & Ellis, The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time (CUP 1973) sec. 4.3 -- no arXiv copy; NAMED-NOT-READ. published_statement: WEC: T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi (Curiel p.6; MM&V eq 2.5; K&S eq 18). NEC: T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for every null k (MM&V eq 2.6). SEC: (T_ab - T g_ab/2) xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi (4D; K&S eq 20 gives T/(n-2) in n dims). DEC: T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 AND -T^a_b xi^b causal [future-directed] for every timelike xi, equivalently T_ab t^a xi^b >= 0 for co-oriented timelike t, xi. Implications: 'Clearly, the SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC' (Curiel p.8); 'if the WEC is not satisfied, then the DEC has to be violated. However, the WEC and the SEC are, in principle, completely independent' (MM&V p.3); 'the DEC is just the combination of the WEC and the FEC' (MM&V p.13); 'even though the name suggests it, the SEC does not imply the WEC' (K&S p.9). Type-I effective forms: NEC rho+p_i>=0; WEC + rho>=0; SEC + rho+Sum p_i>=0; DEC |p_i|<=rho, rho>=0 (MM&V p.6).
published_hypotheses: definitions, not theorems: they quantify over ALL timelike (resp. null) vectors at a point; 'hold' needs every observer, 'fail' needs one
4-dimensional Lorentzian (M,g), signature (-,+,+,+); the SEC's 1/2 is 1/(n-2) at n=4
DEC in the Hawking-Ellis form includes the WEC clause; the flux-only condition (FEC, MM&V eq 4.3) is a different condition that does NOT imply the WEC
the effective (rho, p_i) forms require Hawking-Ellis type I; the covariant forms need no type assumption
physical form equals geometric form only when the Einstein equation holds (Curiel p.5); T_ab = G_ab in certify.py's units is exactly that identification
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED NAME, certify.py:353-355 dec_holds(wec_min) = wec_min >= 0 is the NECESSARY half of the DEC only; published DEC also needs the flux -T^a_b V^b causal (z3 counterexample: rho=0, p_i=1/2 satisfies WEC, fails DEC). The tree uses it only in the published direction (WEC fails => DEC fails; certify.py:85, :453), and every sampled WEC minimum is negative, so no printed verdict is affected; but the DEC column at certify.py:450 would print 'ok' for a WEC-satisfying, DEC-violating tensor. Discrepancy, not a refutation.

ADDED SAMPLING, certify.py:336-351: published WEC/SEC quantify over all timelike vectors; the tree takes 200 Fibonacci directions x speeds j/11, j=1..10 (the static observer s=0 is not in the sample; the cap s=10/11 excludes s->1). A negative sample is a valid witness of violation (one observer suffices), so 'VIOLATED' stands; the sampled minima are NOT infima: where rho+p<0 the WEC infimum over observers is -infinity (K&S Prop 2.1; Le 2602.18023 sec 2.2; measured here: gamma^2(rho+s^2 p) at r=1 is -4.66e-3 at s=10/11, -4.39e-2 at s=0.99, -4.41e2 at s=0.999999). The tree's own hypothesis list names this ('a sampled minimum, not an infimum').

SEC at certify.py:336-351 uses w + T/2 with T = eta^mn T_mn: machine-checked equal to (T_ab - T g_ab/2)V^aV^b for unit timelike V (sympy); valid at n=4 only, which is the tree's dimension. No drift.

overturn.py:207-213: 'rho < 0 ... means the POINTWISE weak energy condition fails' holds by definition when rho is the energy density T_ab u^a u^b measured by some timelike u; the file's density is a functional, not a solution of the field equations (stated at overturn.py:209-211), so the implicit hypothesis is 'rho is an observer-measured T_ab u^a u^b'. Under that reading no drift; 'flat-space kinematics' is not needed by the implication.

later_literature.what: Table 1 / Fig. 2: DEC => WEC => NEC, SEC => NEC, SEC does not imply WEC; Prop 2.1: a scale-invariant EC bounded below has infimum 0 (so a WEC violation makes the sampled minimum unbounded below); all pointwise ECs are violated by QFT and by nonminimal classical scalars -- a statement about the ECs as physical laws, not about the definitions the tree uses.
DEC = WEC + FEC; FEC alone independent of sign of rho; type I-IV tables; ECs 'provisional' as fundamental physics.
Definitions in geometric/physical/effective forms; 'SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC'; DEC/SDEC effective forms coincide only for type I.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. These are DEFINITIONS and one logical implication; they contain no measured input, so no datum available later can move them. Evidence: the same definitions and the same DEC=>WEC implication are restated unchanged in 2014, 2017, 2020 and 2026 (sources above), and DEC=>WEC is re-derived here by z3 (type I) and by a covariant sampled check (no type assumption). What later work DID add is about the ECs' status as physical constraints -- violation by quantum fields (K&S sec 2.3, 'all pointwise energy conditions are necessarily violated by essentially any QFT'), abandonment of the trace EC after Zel'dovich (MM&V p.3-5) -- and about how to test them numerically (Le 2026). Neither bears on the tree's use: certify.py and overturn.py use the ECs as diagnostics of a given T_ab and certify only violations, which need one witness. Evidence the other way: none found; no later paper revises the definitions or the implication.
grade_evidence: Published definitions (via Curiel 2014, MM&V 2017, K&S 2020 restating Hawking-Ellis 1973) match certify.py's NEC (k=(1,u)), WEC, SEC (w + T/2, sympy-verified at n=4) and the direction of 'the DEC requires the WEC' actually used (WEC fails => DEC fails; z3-valid, covariant check 0/234 exceptions). The violation claims certify.py:84-85 rests on are reproduced from an independent exact sympy Einstein tensor at all six radii and, in closed form, extended to every 0<r<R_s. Recorded discrepancies, none a refutation and none moving the conclusion: dec_holds() is named as the DEC but is only its necessary WEC half (certify.py:353-355); sampled minima are not infima (named by the tree); certify.py:96-97 quotes the coordinate T_00 (-4.8455e-4, ratio 1.21) where the orthonormal value is -4.6564e-4 (ratio 1.1655), and the selftest at :456 cannot see it because near() is absolute-tolerance below |want| = 1 (:411). SEAT_LEAD_SPLIT_SURVIVES = False is unaffected: it rests on the sign of the violations, which is exact.
